analysis.title: Asia Open - Fed up
key_insights: Hawkish Fedspeak and Trump's dismissal of an Iran deal sent oil higher and extended the repricing of the Fed path. OIS prices a 73% probability of a January hike, up from 25% before Tuesday's CPI print.
USTs bear flattened. 2y yields rose about 14bps to 4.881% and 10y rose 13bps to 5.125%, the highest since about mid-October. The 10y broke above 5.10%.
The dollar strengthened across all major pairs. EURUSD hit a fresh YTD low of 1.1046 and CHF led gains among peers as a haven.

USDJPY briefly broke above 160 (intraday high 160.05) and reversed to 159.33, with no signs of intervention. Citi G10 FX strategy flags intervention risk around 160 and says policymakers may seek to push USDJPY back toward 155 if yen weakness becomes disorderly. Support is the 100dma (158.99) then the 200dma (158.72).
Citi Japan Economics expects the BoJ to hike in December in its base case.

Equity indices were resilient (SPX -35bps, NDX -30bps) while RTY fell 1.7% on rate sensitivity. More than 350 SPX constituents closed lower. Nvidia fell 4.5% after CEO Jensen Huang's resignation, with rotation into AMD (+6%), Broadcom (+6%) and Arista (+5%).

Index vols were firm (Jan ATM SPX +0.2v, QQQ +0.1v, IWM -0.35v). Customer flow sold index options, unwinding SPX downside hedges and selling QQQ upside, mostly Nov-Dec expiries. Semis vols were bid more in single names than in SMH.
Brent gained about 3.5-4% to $96.13, above its 100dma (94.99) and 200dma (94.22), after Trump said 'Those days have long since passed' on an Iran deal.

Gold fell nearly 3% to a fresh 52-week low amid broad de-risking. Citi's Rui Ding flags the 100WMA, which has held since 2022 apart from a false break in Oct 2023, as in danger of breaking. Citi sales see physical demand re-emerging below the $3875-3900/oz area, with central bank buying returning if funding costs and sovereign stress indicators stabilize.
The $25B 30-year auction tailed the 1pm market level by 0.4bp at 5.441%, with a bid/cover of 2.36 (18th percentile of the past 12 auctions).
Jobless claims were 200k vs 194k estimate. Continuing claims of 1697k imply the unemployment rate could fall to about 3.9%-4.0% in early 2027, per Citi economists.

Citi economists expect Friday's PPI headline below consensus at +0.3% MoM, but say it is unlikely to change expectations for a December/January Fed hike even though it is the last inflation print before the meeting.

USDBRL rose 1.3% to 5.64, BRL's weakest since June 2025. The market lacks confidence in the new fiscal package (said to save 0.5% of GDP). IPCA was +0.14% MoM vs +0.25% estimate. The Citi trader prefers to stay flat because the setup lacks risk reversals.
Peru's central bank decides on the reference rate at 23:00 GMT. It has held since September 2025. Analysts expect a hike while the market is split between a hike and a pause.
Citi's G10 FX strategy desk re-entered a short EURNOK trade by buying a 2m EURNOK 10.35 put, on the view that US midterm results will not materially reduce Middle East escalation risk.

AMD rose about 6% as a potential beneficiary of rotation out of Nvidia.
Broadcom rose about 6% as a potential beneficiary of rotation out of Nvidia.
Arista rose about 5% as a potential beneficiary of rotation out of Nvidia.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from 25% before Tuesday's CPI print. Front-end yields repriced sharply higher.

macro_indicators.reading: +0.3% MoM (Citi economists); consensus 0.4% MoM vs 1.3% prior
macro_indicators.interpretation: Citi expects a below-consensus print, but the report says it is unlikely to change Fed hike expectations.

macro_indicators.indicator: US PPI ex food and energy (October)
macro_indicators.interpretation: The last inflation print before the Fed meeting.
Citi economists say it implies the unemployment rate could fall to about 3.9%-4.0% in early 2027.
Slightly below Citi's 3.6% full-year forecast, with risks skewed to the upside.
Supports the yen medium term. Intervention risk is flagged near USDJPY 160.

trade_ideas.description: Short EURNOK via buying a 2m EURNOK 10.35 put (re-entered)
trade_ideas.rationale: The desk believes US midterm results will not materially reduce Middle East escalation risk.

trade_ideas.description: Short AUDUSD and AUDJPY (G10 spot trader Pat Hu)
trade_ideas.rationale: Existing position held by the Citi G10 spot trader.

risk_factors: USDJPY at 160 carries intervention risk if yen weakness becomes disorderly.
Further hawkish Fed repricing and rising yields (10y above 5.10%) pressure rate-sensitive equities such as RTY.
Escalation in the Middle East and the end of Iran deal prospects push oil higher.
Weak equity breadth, with more than 350 SPX constituents lower.
Gold's 100WMA is at risk of breaking.
Brazil fiscal credibility, with the market doubting the new package's implementation.
charts_described: Chart of the Day (G10 FX Strategy): the JPY's upward reaction to the correction in Japanese equities has been limited, because the JPY appreciation in August and September had already led the equity correction.
vol_and_positioning: Jan ATM implied vol: SPX +0.2v, QQQ +0.1v, IWM -0.35v.
Derivatives desk flow: vols bid. Customers sold index options, unwinding SPX downside hedges and selling QQQ upside, mostly Nov-Dec expiries.
Semis vols were bid, more in single names than in SMH, given dispersion in price performance.
eFX flows: net inflows leaned toward AUD, NOK and PLN. Leveraged accounts bought MXN and sold ZAR. Outflows led in SEK.
USDBRL flow came mainly from offshore accounts (RM and CTAs), with the setup lacking risk reversals.
geopolitical: President Trump said 'we don't need a deal with Iran' and 'Those days have long since passed', a day after the NYT reported Vice President Vance was open to direct talks with Iranian hardliner Rezaei.
Citi's Deirdre Dunn and former National Security Advisor Stephen Hadley discussed the Iran conflict heading into 2027.
The Citi G10 FX desk believes US midterm election results will not materially reduce Middle East escalation risk.
